candidates.title: JPMorgan and Hyundai Card let AI agents trade with no human involved, inside a box of hard limits
candidates.summary: JPMorgan's Kinexys unit and Hyundai Card ran a simulated foreign-exchange trade carried out by AI agents end to end, with no person in the loop. Kinexys's framework restricts each agent to predefined parameters and automatically rejects anything beyond its authorised limit (an agent cleared for $5 million is blocked above it). Testing with several interacting agents is planned for the first half of 2027; no commercial date.
candidates.why_it_matters: A bank writing an agent's mandate as machine-enforced limits, and saying the obstacle is governance and accountability, not technology: reach, mandate and gap in one sentence.

quote.text: You are going to draw a box around the agent.
quote.by: Wee Kee Toh, global head of Kinexys Insights, quoted by CNBC

importance.reason: Agents moving money with no human, under explicit limits; two days old.

candidates.title: Visa readies 85 European payment firms for purchases made by AI agents, Portugal's Unicre among them
candidates.summary: Visa extended its Agentic Ready programme to merchants' side of payments, starting with more than 85 European participants (Adyen, Stripe, PayPal, Worldline, Checkout.com and Portugal's Unicre among them), on top of 40 issuers already in it. Participants test how AI agents are recognised and authenticated, and how their transactions are processed and protected against fraud; more are expected to join through 2027.
candidates.why_it_matters: The rails for agents that pay are being laid in Europe now, with a Portuguese processor in the first group: who authenticates the agent is where its mandate gets checked.
claims_to_check: Visa's own release for the partner list

importance.reason: Agentic payments in Europe with a Portuguese participant; one day old.

photo.description: Gonçalo Santos Lopes, Visa's country manager in Portugal

candidates.title: ChatGPT gets a Wallet so its agents can shop and check out for you
candidates.summary: OpenAI launched a Wallet in ChatGPT that lets its agents complete purchases, first for a limited number of US ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and over. It comes a week after OpenAI let businesses run their own agents inside ChatGPT.
candidates.why_it_matters: Agents that hold a means of payment: the EU's Digital Fairness Act proposal (purchase approval, sponsored suggestions) is aimed squarely at this.
claims_to_check: Open the article and OpenAI's announcement: controls on spending and approval

importance.reason: Big launch but six days old and US-only.

candidates.title: Apple adds Mac security controls aimed at AI agents acting across files and apps
candidates.summary: Apple announced security changes for macOS 27.3 aimed at AI agents, which unlike chatbots run on the device and can act across the operating system, files and apps on the user's behalf.
candidates.why_it_matters: The operating system starts to define what an agent may reach on a personal machine: the reach of the reach, mandate and gap triad.
claims_to_check: Open the article and Apple's own notes for what the controls are

importance.reason: Platform-level controls for agents; three days old.

candidates.title: European Commission hit by attackers using ARTEX, an AI tool that runs fleets of hacking agents
candidates.summary: Hackers using ARTEX, a publicly available AI-powered penetration-testing framework (per Politico's sources), targeted the European Commission's internal IT, causing over ten days of disruption: Sysper (payslips, timesheets, leave) and MyPMO (medical reimbursements) were taken offline, and staff personal data may have been exposed. ARTEX's developer pulled it from GitHub in October but forks spread; CERT-EU warned of ARTEX-assisted attacks on 5 November, and the FBI says researchers found over 1,600 ARTEX consoles exposed online, with some attacks reaching privileged access in under three hours.
candidates.why_it_matters: Agents with no mandate at all, aimed at the institution writing Europe's AI rules: the gap at its widest, the week after the AI Act's enforcement powers took effect.

quote.text: Individual systems were targeted and, in line with our standard practice, we have informed those concerned.
quote.by: Thomas Regnier, Commission spokesperson, quoted via Politico by The Register

claims_to_check: The ARTEX attribution is Politico's sources, reported by The Register: check the Commission, CERT-EU's 5 November warning and the FBI advisory
Whether staff data was accessed: not said by the Commission

importance.reason: A same-day agentic cyberattack on the European Commission itself.

candidates.title: OpenAI opens its Daybreak cyber-defence tool to NATO and European governments; ENISA finds four flaws in EU software
candidates.summary: OpenAI gave NATO's Communications and Information Agency, France, Germany and Poland access to Daybreak, which lets defence teams use its models to audit software and find and patch flaws; Ukraine uses it to protect civilian infrastructure. ENISA used the models to find four vulnerabilities in software used by EU institutions, and in a joint report with CERT-EU on 27 projects 95% of 88 reported issues were real bugs.
candidates.why_it_matters: The defensive side of the same week: agents used under human oversight to find flaws before attackers' agents do, and a US lab inside Europe's cyber defence, a sovereignty question too.
claims_to_check: ENISA and CERT-EU's joint report (the 4 flaws, 88 issues, 95%)

importance.reason: European institutions adopting agentic cyber defence; two days old; pairs with the Commission attack.
